fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled Mach-O header bytes are read from the input file into mhdri; fields ncmds=2 and sizeofcmds=72 are taken from these bytes.
ncmds=2 from the header drives how many load-command iterations the loop below performs.
headway is initialized to sizeofcmds=72 and tracks the remaining bytes of the load-command area.
A heap buffer of exactly sizeofcmds (72) bytes is allocated (76 bytes of malloc under ASan) and filled with the load-command bytes from the file.
ptr walks the load commands; the advance is the previous command's cmdsize (72 == sizeofcmds), so after command 0 ptr lands exactly at the end of the 72-byte rawmseg_buf.
Iteration j=1: get_le32 reads 4 bytes at ptr (offset 72..76 of the 76-byte ASan allocation), so this read is still in-bounds and no error is reported yet.
get_le32 reads 4 bytes at ptr+4 == rawmseg+76, past the 72-byte rawmseg_buf and past the 76-byte ASan allocation: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 4 in get_ne32 (bele.h).

The only bounds guard runs AFTER the 8-byte Mach_command header has already been read, and it only checks headway < cmdsize for the current command; it never requires the >= 8 bytes needed for the next command header, so a command whose cmdsize consumes all of sizeofcmds (headway becomes 0) lets the next unguarded header read go out of bounds. Safety condition that should hold: headway >= 8 before reading the next header.
